name: minised
why: A tiny sed implementation is a close call, interesting as a minimal Unix stream editor but still a fairly plain utility.

brief.what_it_is: minised is a small, stream-oriented implementation of the Unix sed stream editor, written in C. The ExactCODE homepage describes it as a smaller, cheaper, faster SED implementation. The page does not describe its inputs and outputs in detail. As a sed, it is a filter that reads text and applies editing scripts to it. The homepage gives no usage examples.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's framing is embedded use: they needed a tiny sed for use with dietlibc and found Eric S. Raymond's sed implementation useful, but it had bugs and was no longer maintained. After sending fixes, they took over maintenance of the code.
brief.install_notes: The page lists no install steps. Source is said to be a work-in-progress Subversion repository at http://svn.exactcode.de/minised/trunk, and release tarballs are listed on the page. Distribution packages are listed for T2 SDE. The page does not mention Homebrew, a build command, or a license.
brief.standout: It is a small sed built for embedded and static-libc use, with a test suite added. The page says the maintainers fixed bugs, added missing features, and improved POSIX conformance. It is also a historic lineage: the page says Minix uses it and that GNU used to.
brief.status: Maintained, with evidence on the page. The most recent release listed is minised-1.16.tar.gz from 8 October 2021. Earlier releases are dated 2014, 2013, 2009, and 2006, with older ones going back to 1995. The page says the project is being maintained, but it gives no current commit date.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not say what license the code uses. The main source is a Subversion repository served over plain http, and the page calls it work-in-progress. The page is also thin on usage, so a reader has to go to the tarball or source for details. The Homebrew formula's description and executable name (minised) are the only Homebrew-specific information I had, and the page does not describe the executable.
quotes: A smaller, cheaper, faster SED implementation
Mini-sed is a smaller, cheaper, faster SED implementation. Minix uses it. GNU used to use it, until they built their own sed around an extended (some would say over-extended) regexp package.
we agreed to continue maintaining this lovely, historic sed implementation.
fetch_log: https://exactcode.com/opensource/minised/ - fetched OK; the page is the project's homepage and has the full description, release list, and source pointer. No README or docs link was followed, since the page itself covered the material and the SVN link was the only other reference.
